- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent mean to avoid undershoot.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add slight downward slope.
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add a slight upward bias (1–3%) to counteract downward drift.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to overfit recent volatility; use 3–5 day moving average to smooth forecast and avoid overreaction to short-term noise.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates downward trends in low-sentiment periods; increase forecast floor by 1–3% if sentiment < -0.3 for 5+ consecutive days.
- If sentiment is positive and price is rising, model often overestimates upside; cap forecast at +5% above recent 10-day high to avoid overbought bias.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment when price is near support/resistance; if sentiment is strong and price is near recent low, add 1–2% upward bias to avoid missing reversal.
